sources.title: T. Hastie, A. Montanari, S. Rosset, and R. Tibshirani, Surprises in High-Dimensional Ridgeless Least Squares Interpolation
sources.locator: Full 68-page paper. Read §§2.1–2.4, 3.1–3.3, and Appendix C.2; the local authoring uses the minimum-norm definition and risk formulas while proving the stated finite-fourth extension from the current local RMT supplier.

contents.name: Section 2.1 Definition 1 and Proposition 1: ridgeless minimum-norm least-squares solution
contents.reason: The source definition is recorded using X^+y, and the equivalent minimum-norm least-squares characterization is checked against the published pseudoinverse theorem.

contents.name: Proposition 1: pseudoinverse characterization of the minimum-norm least-squares fit
contents.reason: The complete finite-dimensional result is already published and supplies the exact equivalence used by the new estimator definition.

contents.name: Theorem 1 and Theorem 2: underparameterized and overparameterized asymptotic risk formulas
contents.reason: The paper supplies the formula and model context. The authored claim keeps the controlling local real finite-fourth nested-array hypotheses and cites the current RMT risk corollary for that broader moment class.

contents.name: Appendix C.2 proof route for the overparameterized risk
contents.reason: The paper's Appendix C.2 argument assumes an 8+delta moment and uses a different random-matrix route; the local proof does not import it as evidence for the finite-fourth extension.

contents.name: Section 3.2 signal-to-noise regimes and overparameterized risk curve
contents.reason: The risk components and derivative thresholds are derived from the locally proved component limits; the source discussion is used to check the intended signal-to-noise interpretation.

sources.title: M. Belkin, D. Hsu, S. Ma, and S. Mandal, Reconciling modern machine learning practice and the bias-variance trade-off
sources.locator: Full 23-page paper. Read §§2–3, Appendix A Theorem 1 and proof sketch, and the Figure 2, Figure 4, and Figure 5 experiment descriptions.

contents.name: Appendix A, Theorem 1: noiseless Gaussian RKHS interpolation on iid uniform samples from a compact cube
contents.reason: The source theorem and its qualifications are retained. Its proof is only a sketch that invokes Wendland (2004), Theorem 11.22, so the local theorem remains escalated until the power-function estimate has a complete proof.

contents.name: Appendix A proof sketch: fill distance and Gaussian RKHS power-function estimate
contents.reason: The grid and union-bound part is proved locally. The Gaussian estimate is recorded as a proposed local supplier, with the cited missing proof chain stated explicitly.

contents.name: Figure 2 and Section 2: random Fourier feature double-descent experiment
contents.reason: The finite MNIST experiment, class count, feature count, interpolation threshold, and empirical-only scope are recorded in the example.

contents.name: Figure 4: fully connected two-layer neural-network double-descent experiment
contents.reason: The example records the reported sample count, input dimension, output count, and observed nK parameter threshold without elevating it to a general theorem.

contents.name: Figure 5 and Section 3: random-forest double-descent experiment
contents.reason: The example records the reported sample count and the joint maximum-leaves/tree-count complexity index as an empirical observation.

contents.name: Small-norm inductive-bias mechanism for richer random-feature classes
contents.reason: This discussion is a proposed explanatory mechanism rather than a general proved claim; the assigned example records only the source's finite experimental evidence.

sources.title: C. E. Rasmussen and C. K. I. Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning
sources.locator: Full 22-page chapter. Read §6.1 (printed pp. 129–132) for the RKHS and Moore–Aronszajn conventions, and §6.2.1 (printed pp. 133–135) for the stationary squared-exponential kernel formula.

contents.name: Section 6.1: reproducing kernel Hilbert space definition and Moore–Aronszajn theorem
contents.reason: The textbook fixes the real RKHS and reproducing-property conventions used by the local interpolation reduction.

contents.name: Section 6.2.1: Fourier representation of the squared-exponential kernel
contents.reason: The source confirms the Gaussian kernel convention. Its Fourier formula does not supply the missing fill-distance power-function estimate.

contents.name: Section 6.2 representer-theorem and regularized-solution discussion
contents.reason: The assigned noiseless bound applies to every interpolant in the same RKHS and does not require a representer or positive-ridge minimizer argument.

sources.title: C. Rieger and B. Zwicknagl, Sampling inequalities for infinitely smooth functions, with applications to interpolation and machine learning
sources.locator: Full 27-page article PDF. Read Theorem 6.1 and its complete proof, §§4.2–4.5 (including Theorems 4.5 and 4.3), and the proof dependency for the Gaussian fill-distance power-function estimate.

contents.name: Theorem 6.1 with lambda=0: Gaussian interpolation error estimate on a cube
contents.reason: The estimate is preserved as the exact proposed local supplier. The complete inspected proof route invokes earlier sampling inequalities. Its compact-cube route depends on local polynomial reproduction based on Madych and Nelson (1992), Lemma 1, whose proof is not reproduced; the separate general-domain route cites Wendland (2001).

contents.name: Theorem 4.5 and Theorem 4.3 cube route with local polynomial reproduction
contents.reason: The compact-cube route uses local polynomial reproduction based on Madych and Nelson (1992), Lemma 1, without reproducing its proof; the separate general-domain route invokes Wendland (2001). The Gaussian power-function prerequisite remains unresolved.

contents.name: Theorem 7.5 Gaussian Sobolev embedding
contents.reason: The theorem is not needed for the fixed Gaussian-kernel power-function bound or the iid uniform fill-distance calculation in this assigned pair.
